response.title: My HOA bans generators and propane. What battery setup can run my fridge and a few lights for several days?
response.answer:
For an HOA that bans generators and propane, I'd recommend a LiFePO₄ (lithium iron phosphate) portable power station with expandable batteries. It's quiet, produces no exhaust, and can run indoors.

For a refrigerator and a few LED lights over several days, I'd target 5–8 kWh of battery storage, with the option to expand to 10 kWh.

1. How much battery do you need?

Assuming a modern full-size refrigerator, four LED lights, and occasional phone charging:

Appliance

	

Estimated daily energy




Full-size refrigerator

	

1,200–1,800 Wh




Four LED lights, 5 hours

	

160 Wh

50 Wh

150–300 Wh




Total per day

	

1.6–2.3 kWh

Estimated battery capacity by outage duration

2 days

4–5 kWh

3 days

5 days

10–12 kWh
Planning estimates without recharging. Actual consumption depends heavily on the refrigerator, room temperature, and inverter efficiency.

A 2 kWh power station is fine for short outages, but it generally won't keep a typical refrigerator running for three days.

2. Battery systems worth considering
Shop

EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3

My preferred setup

4.096 kWh base, expandable to 8.192 or 12.288 kWh with extra batteries. 4,000W AC output. 
EcoFlow
+1

For your needs: base unit plus one expansion battery.

Shop

Anker SOLIX F3800

3.84 kWh base, 7.68 kWh with one BP3800 expansion battery. High-output system with substantial expansion potential. 
The Home Depot Images
+1

A good alternative if you may eventually want backup for more appliances.

These are both substantial systems, so check their weight and where you would store them before buying.

3. Calculate your backup runtime

Adjust the estimates to see how much capacity you need.

Refrigerator consumption

1,400 Wh/day

Lighting consumption

160 Wh/day

Battery capacity
4.1 kWh — base unit
8.2 kWh — base + expansion
12.3 kWh — base + two expansions

Estimated runtime without recharging

3.9 days

At approximately 1,831 Wh/day

Assumes 75 Wh/day for small devices, 12% overhead, and 88% usable battery capacity. This is an approximation, not a guaranteed runtime.
4. HOA and installation considerations

A portable battery is different from a fuel-powered generator, but some HOAs also restrict equipment marketed as a "solar generator." I'd check the exact wording of your rules before purchasing.

For the simplest arrangement, keep the battery indoors and plug the refrigerator and lights directly into it during an outage. This avoids modifying your home's electrical system.

If you want to power existing wall outlets automatically, you'd need an appropriate transfer switch or backup panel installed by a qualified electrician, along with any required approvals. Never backfeed power through an ordinary wall outlet.

Solar panels can extend runtime if your HOA permits them and you have sufficient sunlight. Without solar or another charging source, your backup duration is limited by stored energy.

Knowing your refrigerator's model number or its annual kWh rating would make the runtime estimate considerably more accurate.
markup:
For an HOA that bans generators and propane, I'd recommend a **LiFePO₄ (lithium iron phosphate) portable power station with expandable batteries**. It's quiet, produces no exhaust, and can run indoors.

For a refrigerator and a few LED lights over several days, I'd target **5–8 kWh of battery storage**, with the option to expand to 10 kWh.

## 1. How much battery do you need?

Assuming a modern full-size refrigerator, four LED lights, and occasional phone charging:

| Appliance | Estimated daily energy |
|---|---:|
| Full-size refrigerator | 1,200–1,800 Wh |
| Four LED lights, 5 hours | 160 Wh |
| Phone charging / small devices | 50 Wh |
| Inverter losses and overhead | 150–300 Wh |
| **Total per day** | **1.6–2.3 kWh** |

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={2}>
  <text weight="medium" size="sm">Estimated battery capacity by outage duration</text>
  <grid columns={3} gap={2}>
    {#each [{d:"2 days",v:"4–5 kWh"},{d:"3 days",v:"6–8 kWh"},{d:"5 days",v:"10–12 kWh"}] as x}
      <grid-item>
        <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} align="center" gap={1}>
          <text color="secondary" size="xs">{x.d}</text>
          <title size="lg" color="default">{x.v}</title>
        </box>
      </grid-item>
    {/each}
  </grid>
  <caption>Planning estimates without recharging. Actual consumption depends heavily on the refrigerator, room temperature, and inverter efficiency.</caption>
</box>

A 2 kWh power station is fine for short outages, but it generally won't keep a typical refrigerator running for three days.

## 2. Battery systems worth considering

<box gap={3}>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 portable power station product white background" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="136px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **<Entity category="product" value="EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3"/>**

      <badge color="success">My preferred setup</badge>

      4.096 kWh base, expandable to 8.192 or 12.288 kWh with extra batteries. 4,000W AC output. <Cite refs={["turn784958search1","turn784958search2"]}/>

      For your needs: base unit plus one expansion battery.
    </box>
  </row>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <row align="start" gap={3}>
    <AsyncImage query="Anker SOLIX F3800 portable power station black wheels product" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="136px" shop_eligible={true}/>
    <box flex="1" gap={1}>
      **<Entity category="product" value="Anker SOLIX F3800"/>**

      3.84 kWh base, 7.68 kWh with one BP3800 expansion battery. High-output system with substantial expansion potential. <Cite refs={["turn784958search12","turn784958product10"]}/>

      A good alternative if you may eventually want backup for more appliances.
    </box>
  </row>
</box>

These are both substantial systems, so check their weight and where you would store them before buying.

## 3. Calculate your backup runtime

Adjust the estimates to see how much capacity you need.

{@body const [fridge,setFridge] = DIL.useState(1400)}
{@body const [lights,setLights] = DIL.useState(160)}
{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState("8192")}
{@body const daily = (fridge+lights+75)*1.12}
{@body const days = Number(capacity)*0.88/daily}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      <text weight="medium" size="sm">Refrigerator consumption</text>
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{fridge.toLocaleString()} Wh/day</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={500} max={2500} step={100} value={fridge} onChange={setFridge}/>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <row justify="between" align="center">
      <text weight="medium" size="sm">Lighting consumption</text>
      <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{lights} Wh/day</text>
    </row>
    <slider min={40} max={500} step={20} value={lights} onChange={setLights}/>
  </box>
  <box gap={1}>
    <label>Battery capacity</label>
    <radio-group direction="col" value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}>
      <radio value="4096">4.1 kWh — base unit</radio>
      <radio value="8192">8.2 kWh — base + expansion</radio>
      <radio value="12288">12.3 kWh — base + two expansions</radio>
    </radio-group>
  </box>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} align="center" gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated runtime without recharging</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{days.toFixed(1)} days</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">At approximately {Math.round(daily).toLocaleString()} Wh/day</text>
  </box>
  <caption>Assumes 75 Wh/day for small devices, 12% overhead, and 88% usable battery capacity. This is an approximation, not a guaranteed runtime.</caption>
</box>

## 4. HOA and installation considerations

A portable battery is different from a fuel-powered generator, but some HOAs also restrict equipment marketed as a "solar generator." I'd check the exact wording of your rules before purchasing.

For the simplest arrangement, keep the battery indoors and plug the refrigerator and lights directly into it during an outage. This avoids modifying your home's electrical system.

If you want to power existing wall outlets automatically, you'd need an appropriate transfer switch or backup panel installed by a qualified electrician, along with any required approvals. Never backfeed power through an ordinary wall outlet.

Solar panels can extend runtime if your HOA permits them and you have sufficient sunlight. Without solar or another charging source, your backup duration is limited by stored energy.

## 5. Two questions to narrow this down

{@body const [budget,setBudget] = DIL.useState("3000-5000")}
{@body const [duration,setDuration] = DIL.useState("3")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Recommend a specific HOA-friendly indoor battery backup setup for my refrigerator and a few lights. My budget is "+budget+" USD and I need "+duration+" days of backup without recharging. Include a parts list and approximate total price.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What's your total budget?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={budget} onChange={setBudget}>
        <radio value="under 1500">Under $1,500</radio>
        <radio value="1500-3000">$1,500–$3,000</radio>
        <radio value="3000-5000">$3,000–$5,000</radio>
        <radio value="over 5000">$5,000+</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>How long do you want to run without recharging?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={duration} onChange={setDuration}>
        <radio value="2">2 days</radio>
        <radio value="3">3 days</radio>
        <radio value="5">5 days</radio>
        <radio value="7">7 days</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Find my ideal battery setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

Knowing your refrigerator's model number or its annual kWh rating would make the runtime estimate considerably more accurate.
